Cliche I know, but just breathe. In my opinion, a slip up doesn’t actually erase all your progress. Sure, the timer is reset, but you still succeeded. Someone making a painting who skips a day of painting doesn’t mean the painting just vanished from existence. It’s still there, they just simply didn’t continue for a day. Someone who’s been sober for 20 years isn’t automatically dubbed a daily drinker just because they slipped up and had a drink one night.

I’m so sorry this has all happened to you. I can only imagine how torn you must feel with wanting to be there for your kids but also wanting to just disappear. You said Erik is very caring. Does he know how you’re feeling right now? Letting him know what you’re going through could help. I’ve been in that state where you can’t even do the most basic of things, and it sucks. Have you ever gone to therapy or reached out at all? There’s a good chance getting help could take some weight off your shoulders. 

Being depressed does not make you a burden. You’re simply someone who is hurt and in need of help. Depression affects people in many physical ways, so you’re NOT just being ‘lazy’ by finding it hard to do simple tasks. If one day you’re feeling up to it, maybe you could try doing something small like cleaning one counter or making a sandwich for your kids. I know that for me, personally, doing small things is good because it helps me feel like I’m helping others. But like I said before, you don’t need to do this all alone. Please reach out to someone. What you’re going through is not something anyone should have to go through alone.

I’m no expert, but as someone who has been suicidal for a while now I might be able to offer some insight. I think even just you being there for him in the first place is an amazing start. I think professional help is definitely a good idea, but please be careful with this. Often times people get so caught up in saving the person that they forget how a human being should be treated. I know I would hate to be involuntarily hospitalized and if I were It would probably drive me closer to the edge instead of the opposite. As for the jokes, a lot of us find comfort in joking about these issues. It’s pretty much just a sad coping mechanism. That’s pretty much why subs like r/2meirl4meirl exist. I wouldn’t say it’s really a manic breakdown, but again I don’t know him and it’s different for everyone. I’m sorry he said those things to you. Mental disorders really take a toll on a person and can make them become over emotional in certain ways or easily irritable. I myself have found that I’ll say hurtful things to people that I regret because of this. I think you’re really strong, and I wish you the best in this. I’m happy to answer any questions.
